beats.narration: A club media office must publish the match report in four languages; one wrong number goes out under the club's name. Agon: Microsoft Foundry agents write, code checks, the officer approves in Teams.

visual.actions: video/stills/opening.html recorded as a clip, its CSS animation rewound at the lead: the title and what Agon is, the problem, then the flow of one run as boxes that appear one after another

beats.narration: A real run: the approval card arrives in the club's Teams channel, with the report the officer attests.

visual.actions: the approval card arrives in the Match Day channel; the officer did not ask for it

beats.narration: The match is synthetic, from our own seeded league. Home and away are clear at a glance, and Agon's interpret model turns the event log into expected goals, pressure and win probability.

visual.actions: Match Centre at 375 px on the recorded run's match (its seed picked in Match setup): the scoreboard and replay at 60x, then the win probability chart and team stats that agon.interpret computes (lane D4)

facts.text: [Cc]omputed by agon\.interpret from the synthetic event log

beats.narration: In a Microsoft Agent Framework workflow, Microsoft Foundry agents pick the turning points and write the report. Code checks every claimed number, name and minute against the event log; a failing sentence goes back to the writer once before the officer sees anything.

visual.actions: Newsroom Wall at 1920 on the recorded run: Replay the run, so each desk fills step by step, to the Fact Gate verdict

facts.text: Recomputed every number, name and minute the headline report claims from the event log, and matched every number written in digits to a claim: pass
Fact Gate: pass, as sealed in the bundle manifest
a Fact Gate mismatch: one retry through the Writer, then a template line with corrected claims
add_flag\(d, "factgate_retry", f"sent back to the Writer once
recompute every claimed number, name, minute and score from the event log
A number in the\s+prose that no claim carries is a mismatch

beats.narration: The officer asks for nothing: the card is already in the channel. They read the report they attest, tick the Confirm row the code cannot check, and approve.

visual.actions: the officer reads the attested report, ticks the Confirm row (the card refuses an approval without it), taps Approve

beats.narration: While the card waited, the worker process ended. The approval woke a new one, which resumed from the durable checkpoint and published exactly once.

visual.actions: a timeline drawn from evidence/<run>.executions.json: the first worker process ends, the card waits, the intake verifies, a new worker resumes, one publish (until the operations view is live)

beats.narration: The same card now says what was published and what was only prepared or recorded. One approval covers every edition: Greek, Spanish, French and easy-read.

visual.actions: the card updated in place: Published to, Prepared as a preview, not posted, Recorded for sending, Not sent, as you chose
Recap at 1920: the EN, EL, ES, FR and Easy-read edition tabs in turn

beats.narration: Anyone can check it. Every file is hashed again in your browser, and the approved hash equals the published hash.

visual.actions: open Verify at 1920 so the recomputation runs on camera, then bring the recorded run's approved and published comparison into view

facts.text: Recomputed in your browser: the bundle hash equals the hash on the approval card
(\d+) of \1 published files match the sealed manifest
Recomputed in your browser: (\d+) of \1 files match\.
The approved hash equals the published hash

beats.narration: Take Foundry out and no report exists. Take the checkpoint out and an approval cannot survive a restart. Take Teams out and nothing publishes. Agon: the demo and the code are linked below.
